reasoningObjective: By the end of this chapter, students should be better able to trace and evaluate a data path in order to judge whether a data-driven action respects context, agency, and contestability.

checkpoints.title: Judge the first data path
checkpoints.trigger: What should the college do with Rosa's traces?
checkpoints.prompt: Make a provisional judgment about using Rosa's course data for an early-alert system. Identify one trace the college may use and one limit or condition that would make that use more or less defensible, then explain why.
checkpoints.guidance: Commit before the chapter supplies its full data-path vocabulary. Focus on a concrete use of a trace, not on the general claim that data or AI is good or bad.
checkpoints.rationale: The opening establishes Rosa's partial record and the possibility of a dashboard or intervention before the chapter explains how traces become categories, proxies, and actions.

checkpoints.title: Test the same signal at different stakes
checkpoints.trigger: When does a login pattern become too thin for the action it supports?
checkpoints.prompt: Use Rosa's login frequency as the same signal in two cases: a friendly outreach message and a high-stakes judgment about her motivation or readiness. Explain why the proxy may be defensible in one case and overreach in the other, naming the feature that changes the ethical stakes.
checkpoints.guidance: Keep the signal fixed. Your comparison should show how the action, likely error, or opportunity to correct the record changes what the proxy can reasonably support.
checkpoints.rationale: The passage has established that a proxy can be useful and weak at once, and it contrasts supportive outreach with settled judgments about a person, enabling a disciplined one-feature comparison.

checkpoints.title: Reconcile the data path
checkpoints.trigger: What would make Rosa's data path defensible now?
checkpoints.prompt: Classify your opening judgment as changed, qualified, strengthened, or unchanged. Identify the chapter claim or distinction that caused—or failed to cause—that movement, give your strongest reason now about the early-alert system, and state the most serious remaining uncertainty about its purpose, proxy, or contestability.
checkpoints.guidance: An unchanged view is legitimate if you explain why the chapter's strongest pressure did not dislodge it. Identify a condition the institution would need to satisfy rather than giving only a general verdict.
checkpoints.rationale: The chapter has assembled a defensible data path from clear purpose, proportionate records, contextual integrity, disciplined proxies, visible burdens, and correction routes before the later practice exercise.
